- **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/data-model-rules.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/organization-scope.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/backfill-sys-record-share-organizations.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **153** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b1676441ba59cc32682ffd41e63e74474ad7fa42` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `43bd3b8cb97746bb1f66e5984e31b947d6e669de` — the merge of head `e2b88d857238a1dae999df2c271a73cadae160ef` into base `b1676441ba59cc32682ffd41e63e74474ad7fa42`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 43bd3b8cb97746bb1f66e5984e31b947d6e669de && git checkout 43bd3b8cb97746bb1f66e5984e31b947d6e669de
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b1676441ba59cc32682ffd41e63e74474ad7fa42 e2b88d857238a1dae999df2c271a73cadae160ef && git checkout -B drift-repro b1676441ba59cc32682ffd41e63e74474ad7fa42 && git merge --no-ff e2b88d857238a1dae999df2c271a73cadae160ef

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b1676441ba59cc32682ffd41e63e74474ad7fa42
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b1676441ba59cc32682ffd41e63e74474ad7fa42` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

The body's `Clause-②` parenthetical and its line "No accept set, served body, error code or runtime behaviour moves" are stale. They read as follows:

- The Acceptance-notes bullet on `memory-http-outbox` is a "Fixed here" item.

Withdrawn from this part: the `plugin-auth` organization-less readers (`last-admin-guard.ts` `anchorOwnerTest`, `ensure-default-organization.ts`). They are live contracts, not dead readers, and are filed as #24883.

### ① Derived judgments

**1. The gate — `scripts/check-tenant-chokepoint.mjs` — executes ADR-0131 D8, with no new gate.** D8 (ADR-0131:585-586) names this gate and this refusal; AGENTS.md's default-no for new gates does not apply.

- *Recall over the three SqlDriver-family files.* The rule (`nullArmOf`, :391-422) refuses each Knex spelling that compiles to IS NULL on a tenant column reference: `whereNull` / `orWhereNull` / `andWhereNull` (:395); `where` / `orWhere` / `andWhere` with a null comparand, two- or three-argument (:397); the object form with an identifier, string or computed tenant key (:400-409); and `whereRaw` / `orWhereRaw` / `andWhereRaw` / `havingRaw` / `raw` whose literal says `IS NULL` and names the column by substitution, binding or literal (:411-419). A tenant column reference (`isTenantRef`, :357-370) is a local bound to `this.resolveTenantField` / `computeTenantField` / `computeAndRecordTenantField`, anything named `tenantField`, or the literal `'organization_id'`, unwrapped through parentheses, `!`, `as` and `String()`. Those are the only three ways the scanned files name the column: `sql-driver.ts` binds the resolver at :7657, :8932, :8968, :9721, :12251, :12348, :13874, :15637, :15709, :15747, :17769 and names `tenantField` as a parameter (:7997) and a member (:8368); no other tenant-column name occurs in the three files (grep for tenantColumn / orgField / organizationField / tenancyField is empty), and `sqlite-wasm-driver.ts` and `turso-driver.ts` carry no NULL spelling and no tenant predicate at all. Bindings are scoped to the outermost container (`nullArmsOf`, :455-459), so nested closures are covered. Two blind spots, both outside the drivers' spellings: an element-access verb (`qb[...'orWhereNull' : 'whereNull'](field)`, as the filter compiler writes it at :16683, :17595, :17600 on a filter field) is not a property access and is never examined (:392); a tenant column handed to a helper under a parameter not named `tenantField` is unseen, which the header names (:145-148).
- *Precision on non-tenant columns.* The live NULL spellings in `sql-driver.ts` are the filter compiler's — `whereNull(field)` (:16689, :17113), the null-safe negative raw `IS NULL OR` (:16311) and the distinct-from raws (:17881-17918) — none on a tenant reference, and the silent counterparts at :897-912 mirror exactly those shapes. The gate ran green on the merged tree in the `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` lane. One over-refusal in principle: `where(tenantRef, 'is not', null)` and `where(tenantRef, '=', null)` would be refused because :397 does not read the operator, while header :136 says IS NOT NULL is never refused. Neither spelling exists in the files; the direction is safe.
- *D7 partition.* `NULL_ARM_EXEMPT` (:319) is empty and needs no entry: the surviving NULL disjunct is `globalPassSelector` in `packages/objectql/src/lifecycle/lifecycle-service.ts:272-276`, which keeps `{ [column]: null }` only for `ATTRIBUTION_PARTITION_COLUMNS` (`sys_audit_log.tenant_id`, an ADR-0131 D7 attribution field, ADR:509-511). It is outside `SCAN_FILES` (:168-172), so the header's statement (:138-143) is exact.
- *Floor.* `TENANT_PREDICATE_FLOOR = 3` (:220) has been 3 since the first commit 584b2029; it never read 4. "4 on main" (:216) is the measured count: `sql-driver.ts:8001` (`where(tenantField, tenantId)`), :8368 (`where(reservation.tenantField, …)`), :15652 (`whereIn(field, …)`) and :15664 (`where(field, String(tenantId))`), identical at the branch base df8bb40a and at the head; the subclasses add none. 7a-1 retired an `orWhereNull` arm, which `TENANT_PREDICATE_CALLS` (:310, `where` / `whereIn`) never counted, so no arm retirement moved the count. The floor sits one below the count the way `DISCOVERED_FLOOR = 15` sits below 24 bindings: losing either half of `isTenantRef` (by-name or resolver-bound) drops the count to 2 and exits 2 (:1063-1072). Not a weakening.
- *Self-test and ablation.* The `D8 null-arm rule` battery is 11 refused spellings (:811-875) + 6 silent counterparts (:880-913) + 2 counter asserts (:921-928) + 3 exemption asserts (:931-942) = 22, equal to the pinned floor (:632); the roster floor is 2 (:637). Refused case 1 is the v17 arm itself inside `applyTenantScope`. The ablation recorded in the PR body (the repo's `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, on main since c4b84ad702, run on a scratch copy) put `.orWhereNull(field)` back beside `sql-driver.ts:15664`, where `field` is bound at :15637 by `this.resolveTenantField(object)` — the matcher's first form — and the gate reported that line and exited 1; the restore was blob-equal. The self-test and the ablation discriminate.
- *Wiring.* `package.json:206` runs `--self-test` then the scan; `.github/workflows/lint.yml:4071-4075` runs `pnpm check:tenant-chokepoint` in lane `lint-ci-engine` (:3141, check-run `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`). The step's `continue-on-error: true` is the lane idiom (:151-153): the closing `Lane verdict` step (:4273-4278, `scripts/ci/lane-verdict.mjs` over `toJSON(steps)`) keeps the red. The lane completed `success` on this head; lint.yml has no paths filter.

**2. The memory-http-outbox fix is correct and matches `SqlHttpOutbox`.** `MemoryHttpOutbox.redeliver` (`memory-http-outbox.ts:218-224`) now refuses when `options.tenantId !== undefined && row.organizationId !== options.tenantId`, so an organization-less row (`organizationId` undefined) is `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` to every tenant-scoped caller and still reachable to a tenant-less one. `SqlHttpOutbox.redeliver` (`sql-http-outbox.ts:510-521`) answers the same two ways through `engine.findOne({ where: { id }, tenantId })`: the driver's `applyTenantScope` compiles `organization_id = :tenant` (`sql-driver.ts:15664`) with no NULL arm, and early-outs when `tenantId` is undefined; `sys_http_delivery`'s `organization_id` is the kernel-provisioned tenant column (objectql registry.ts:598), so the scope applies. Pinned: the replaced case (`http-outbox-organization.test.ts:173-190`) asserts the `HttpRedeliverError` class and the `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` code, that the row is untouched (dead, attempts 1), and that a tenant-less replay still succeeds — strictly more than the old single success assertion. Composition: the only shipped construction is `new SqlHttpOutbox(engine, …)` at `messaging-service-plugin.ts:441`; `new MemoryHttpOutbox(` occurs in 35 test files and nowhere else; the class TSDoc (:26) says "for tests and single-process development". It is a public export (`service-messaging/src/index.ts:166`), which the changeset names.

**3. Texts are accurate after 7a-1 (#24825), 7a-3 (#24828), 7b-3 (#24845) and 7c (#24836).** Each of the 15 runtime files and the `[http]` warning (`http-nodes.ts:277-335`) now says an organization-less row is reached by no tenant-scoped read, which is `applyTenantScope` as it stands; `organization-scope.ts:182-189`'s "check-tenant-chokepoint refuses it" becomes true in this same PR. `backfill-sys-record-share-organizations.ts:259-264` says no runtime path calls the pass: grep finds no non-test caller. `metadata-store.ts:787-790` says the `organizationOutOfWriteReach` branch predates D8 — honest, behaviour unchanged. `cli.mdx:1801` and `seed-tenancy-repair.mdx:305` describe 7b-3 in its own words: the counter refuses an organization-less row wherever `sys_organization` is registered (`ERR_SYSTEM_WRITE_ORGANIZATION_REQUIRED`), `__global__` kept where none is. `schema.mdx:608-621` still documents the `COALESCE(organization_id, '__global__')` bucket as the live mechanism and names its remaining uses (a composition with no organization object, pre-18.x residue) — no claim of NOT NULL at createTable (7b-0) or of plain indexes (7b-1+7b-2), which are not on main. The lint texts (`data-model-rules.ts:596-602`, `rule-explanations.ts:2697-2703`) carry the "wherever the organization object is registered" hedge and keep the COALESCE closure. `SharingRuleRow` (`sharing-service.ts:477-484`): `deploymentWide` is the one member with no `sys_sharing_rule` column; the other members map to the declared fields (`sys-sharing-rule.object.ts:95-267`, `criteria` lifted from `criteria_json` :141) and the system `id` / `created_at` / `updated_at`. `check:generated`: the diff changes no `.describe()` string; the replaced TSDoc strings survive only in CHANGELOGs and `api-surface/contracts.json` carries names, not comments, so nothing regenerates; the dev measured 14 artifacts current and CI's reconcile step passed.

**4. Changeset `.changeset/24583-7z-closing-d8-texts.md`.** The ten `patch` entries are exactly the ten packages with a changed file (names verified against each package.json; scripts/, content/docs and the changeset itself publish nothing). `patch` is right: one bug fix in a released package (AGENTS.md:1085) plus shipped text. `Clause-②: no` with a free parenthetical reads as `no` with no arm on both carriers (`clause2-line.mjs:286-293` flags only a word of the widen/narrow family; "one" and "the" are not). No `(narrowing)` arm is right: the gate narrows what a contributor may write in repo scripts, not a published accept set, and the outbox fix conforms a documented test double to the `IHttpOutbox.redeliver` / `RedeliverOptions` contract (`http-outbox.ts:297-301`, "threaded to the driver as DriverOptions.tenantId"), whose narrowing 7a-1 declared `no (narrowing)` and shipped. The PR body's parenthetical is stale and corrected by the seat's note 6291547374. No other pending changeset is in the diff; `docs/adr/**`, CHANGELOGs and consumed changesets are untouched.

**5. Merge hygiene.** Two merges of `main` (e5f47d90, e2b88d857), both clean: for each, the file set of diff(main parent, merge) equals diff(merge-base of the parents, branch parent). The union of the six non-merge commits' files equals the 24 diff paths. `chore: version packages (#24524)` (06cab4849a) is an ancestor of the merge-base b1676441b, so it contributes nothing to `git diff b1676441b e2b88d857`. The PR diff is this part alone.

**CI on the head.** 41 check-runs, 0 failed (30 success, 6 skipped); `Test Core (1/6)` to `(5/6)` still in progress at the final poll; `Test Core (6/6)`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` and every `Lint ·` lane completed `success`. Nothing blocking; the Test Core shards must finish green before the queue lands it.

### ② Semver level

`patch` × 10 — right. No published accept set, served body or error code of a shipped composition moves; the gate is repo tooling; the `MemoryHttpOutbox` change is a conformance fix to an already-declared narrowing, named for direct embedders in the changeset body.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Withdrawn to #24883, correctly not in this diff: the `plugin-auth` organization-less readers (`last-admin-guard.ts` `anchorOwnerTest`, `ensure-default-organization.ts`), live contracts.
- 7a-2 (#24872) carries `core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts` ~795 ("a null-org row is global").
- Left as honest texts, behaviour unchanged (dev acceptance notes): `organizationOutOfWriteReach` (`metadata-store.ts:784-791`) answers in-reach for an organization-less row D8 put out of reach; `applySysRecordShareOrganizationBackfill` is dead code whose write no longer reaches a NULL row.
- N (next text pass): `events.zod.ts:259-262`, unchanged and adjacent to this PR's hunk, still says every `single`-posture event is organization-less because `postureStampsOrganization` is false there; since ADR-0131 D9 (`system-write-organization.ts:43-57`) derives the Default Organization under `single`, and this PR's own `schema.mdx:611-613` says so, the two texts now disagree.
- N (next text pass): `sys-sharing-rule.object.ts:99` field description "null = global" names the retired reading (7a-3's area).
- N (gate, non-blocking): `nullArmOf:397` reads no operator, so `where(tenantRef, 'is not', null)` would be refused against header :136; and element-access verbs are never examined (:392). Neither spelling is in the driver files. Fix: in the 3-argument form refuse only when the operator literal is `is`; name element access under "What it does NOT see".
